_note: Restricted archive contents. clearance gates who may read; revealsFlags fire narrative state on access. focusCost is what studying the document costs — the Apocrypha is not a reward for reaching Chapter 2, it is a second economy the player spends into. Progress here gates the severance attempt.

documents._note: A founding-era inventory in which the catalyst is a line item with a delivery date, not a stockpile. The quiet one — no revelation, just an invoice.
Every Chair before this one, and a mark against each name in the same hand. The player's predecessor kept the log too. Nobody in this chain was ever in charge either.

A lower-level schematic with an architectural oddity on it — a corridor that goes somewhere the Shaft does not have. Dismissible on first read, which is the point: it is the foreshadowing for the physical entry in the takeover.
Gates step 1 of the finale ('reading between the lines'). Sets nexus-is-traceable, which is what makes the severance attempt selectable at all.

A partial list, in the Nexus's vocabulary, of numbered Facilities. The Chair cannot place the shape of it. Optional, late, and the strongest possible setup for the epilogue — the player who finds this reads the Coryphaeus's status board already knowing what they are looking at.
